name: Biology
description: The study of living things — cells, classification, nutrition, transport, respiration, excretion, reproduction, genetics, ecology, coordination and evolution — for the Nigerian senior secondary curriculum, aligned to WAEC, NECO and JAMB requirements.

topics.name: Cell Biology
topics.summary: The cell as the basic unit of life: its structure, how it divides and how substances move across its membrane.

subtopics.name: Cell Structure and Functions
subtopics.summary: The parts of plant and animal cells and the job each part performs.

objectives.text: Name the main organelles of plant and animal cells
State the function of each cell organelle
Compare plant and animal cells and distinguish prokaryotes from eukaryotes

subtopics.name: Cell Division
subtopics.summary: Mitosis and meiosis: the stages, the chromosome numbers and why each type of division matters.

objectives.text: Describe the stages of mitosis in the correct order
Explain the significance of meiosis in gamete formation
Compare mitosis and meiosis in outcome and chromosome number

subtopics.name: Movement of Substances Across Cells
subtopics.summary: Diffusion, osmosis, plasmolysis and active transport, and how each keeps a cell alive.

objectives.text: Define diffusion, osmosis and active transport
Predict the direction of water movement between solutions of different concentration
Explain turgidity, plasmolysis and haemolysis in terms of osmosis

topics.name: Classification of Living Things
topics.summary: How biologists recognise life and sort the millions of known organisms into an ordered system.

subtopics.name: Characteristics of Living Things
subtopics.summary: The seven life processes that separate living organisms from non-living matter.

objectives.text: List the characteristics of living organisms
Explain each life process with a suitable example
Distinguish living things from non-living things and from viruses

subtopics.name: The Classification Scheme
subtopics.summary: Taxonomic ranks from kingdom to species, binomial nomenclature and the five kingdoms.

objectives.text: State the taxonomic hierarchy from kingdom to species
Apply the rules of binomial nomenclature correctly
Describe the main features of the five kingdoms

subtopics.name: Plant and Animal Groups
subtopics.summary: The main divisions of the plant kingdom and the major invertebrate and vertebrate groups.

objectives.text: Identify the four main plant divisions by their features
Classify common animals into the correct phylum or class
Use diagnostic features to place an unfamiliar organism in a group

topics.name: Nutrition
topics.summary: How autotrophs make food and how heterotrophs obtain, digest and absorb it.

subtopics.name: Modes of Nutrition
subtopics.summary: Autotrophic and heterotrophic nutrition, food classes and the diseases of deficiency.

objectives.text: Distinguish autotrophic from heterotrophic nutrition
Classify feeding relationships as parasitic, saprophytic or symbiotic
Relate food classes and vitamins to their functions and deficiency diseases

subtopics.name: Photosynthesis
subtopics.summary: The raw materials, conditions, stages and products of food manufacture in green plants.

objectives.text: State the word and balanced equations for photosynthesis
Identify the raw materials and conditions necessary for photosynthesis
Describe experiments that test for starch and for the necessity of light
Distinguish the light stage from the dark stage of photosynthesis

subtopics.name: Digestion in Mammals
subtopics.summary: The alimentary canal, its enzymes and how digested food is absorbed and assimilated.

objectives.text: Trace food through the parts of the alimentary canal
Match each digestive enzyme to its substrate and product
Explain how the ileum is adapted for absorption

topics.name: Transport Systems
topics.summary: How water, food, gases and wastes are moved around plants and animals.

subtopics.name: Transport in Plants
subtopics.summary: Xylem, phloem, the transpiration stream and translocation of manufactured food.

objectives.text: Compare the structure and function of xylem and phloem
Explain the path of water from soil to leaf
State the factors that affect the rate of transpiration

subtopics.name: Blood and Its Functions
subtopics.summary: The composition of blood, the job of each component, clotting and blood groups.

objectives.text: Describe the composition of blood and the function of each part
Explain how oxygen and carbon dioxide are carried in blood
Apply the ABO and rhesus systems to safe blood transfusion

subtopics.name: The Heart and Blood Vessels
subtopics.summary: Chambers, valves, double circulation and the differences between arteries, veins and capillaries.

objectives.text: Trace the path of blood through the mammalian heart
Compare arteries, veins and capillaries structurally and functionally
Explain the advantage of a double circulation

topics.name: Respiration
topics.summary: Gaseous exchange surfaces and the release of energy from food in living cells.

subtopics.name: Respiratory Surfaces and Breathing
subtopics.summary: Gaseous exchange surfaces from amoeba to mammals, and the mechanism of breathing in humans.

objectives.text: State the features of an efficient respiratory surface
Match organisms to their respiratory organs
Describe the mechanism of inspiration and expiration in humans

subtopics.name: Aerobic and Anaerobic Respiration
subtopics.summary: How cells release energy with and without oxygen, and the uses of fermentation.

objectives.text: Write equations for aerobic and anaerobic respiration
Compare the energy yield of aerobic and anaerobic respiration
Distinguish respiration from combustion and state uses of fermentation

topics.name: Excretion and Homeostasis
topics.summary: Removing metabolic waste and holding the internal environment steady.

subtopics.name: Excretory Organs and Products
subtopics.summary: The four human excretory organs, their products, and excretion in plants and simple animals.

objectives.text: Define excretion and distinguish it from egestion and secretion
Match each excretory organ to the wastes it removes
Describe excretory structures in plants and simple animals

subtopics.name: The Kidney and Homeostasis
subtopics.summary: Urine formation in the nephron, osmoregulation, temperature control and hormonal feedback.

objectives.text: Describe ultrafiltration and selective reabsorption in the nephron
Explain how ADH controls the water content of blood
Explain how body temperature and blood glucose are regulated

topics.name: Reproduction
topics.summary: How organisms produce new individuals, from binary fission to human pregnancy.

subtopics.name: Asexual and Sexual Reproduction
subtopics.summary: Methods of asexual reproduction, the meaning of sexual reproduction and the merits of each.

objectives.text: Describe the main methods of asexual reproduction
Compare asexual and sexual reproduction in terms of variation
Give the advantages and disadvantages of each type of reproduction

subtopics.name: Reproduction in Flowering Plants
subtopics.summary: Flower structure, pollination, fertilisation, fruit formation and seed dispersal.

objectives.text: Name the parts of a flower and state their functions
Compare wind and insect pollinated flowers
Describe fertilisation, fruit formation and agents of seed dispersal

subtopics.name: Human Reproduction
subtopics.summary: The male and female reproductive systems, the menstrual cycle, fertilisation and pregnancy.

objectives.text: Name the parts of the human reproductive systems and their functions
Describe the menstrual cycle and the hormones that control it
Explain fertilisation, implantation and the role of the placenta

topics.name: Genetics and Variation
topics.summary: How characteristics are passed on, why individuals differ and how humans apply this knowledge.

subtopics.name: Chromosomes, Genes and DNA
subtopics.summary: The physical basis of inheritance and the vocabulary needed to describe it.

objectives.text: Describe the structure of DNA and its relationship to genes
Define gene, allele, genotype, phenotype, dominant and recessive
Explain how chromosome number is maintained across generations

subtopics.name: Mendelian Inheritance
subtopics.summary: Monohybrid crosses, test crosses, Punnett squares and Mendel's laws.

objectives.text: State Mendel's law of segregation and law of independent assortment
Use a Punnett square to predict the offspring of a monohybrid cross
Interpret phenotypic and genotypic ratios from a cross

subtopics.name: Variation and Its Applications
subtopics.summary: Continuous and discontinuous variation, sex determination, blood groups, sickle cell and genetic applications.

objectives.text: Distinguish continuous from discontinuous variation
Explain sex determination and sex linked inheritance in humans
Apply genetics to sickle cell counselling, blood groups and plant breeding

topics.name: Ecology
topics.summary: Organisms and their environment: habitats, feeding relationships, cycles and conservation.

subtopics.name: Ecological Concepts and Factors
subtopics.summary: Habitat, niche, population, community, ecosystem and the factors that shape them.

objectives.text: Define the basic ecological terms and use them correctly
Classify ecological factors as biotic or abiotic
Relate adaptations of organisms to their habitats

subtopics.name: Food Chains and Energy Flow
subtopics.summary: Trophic levels, food webs, pyramids of numbers and energy, and the ten per cent rule.

objectives.text: Construct a food chain and identify each trophic level
Explain why energy decreases along a food chain
Interpret pyramids of numbers, biomass and energy

subtopics.name: Nutrient Cycles and Conservation
subtopics.summary: Carbon and nitrogen cycles, pollution, and conserving Nigeria's natural resources.

objectives.text: Describe the carbon cycle and the nitrogen cycle
Identify sources and effects of air, water and soil pollution
Justify methods of conserving natural resources

topics.name: Nervous and Hormonal Coordination
topics.summary: How animals detect and respond to change using nerves, sense organs and hormones.

subtopics.name: The Nervous System and Sense Organs
subtopics.summary: Neurones, the reflex arc, the central nervous system and the structure of the eye and ear.

objectives.text: Describe the parts of a neurone and the divisions of the nervous system
Trace the pathway of a reflex action through the reflex arc
Relate the parts of the eye and ear to their functions

subtopics.name: Hormonal Coordination
subtopics.summary: Endocrine glands, their hormones, deficiency effects, and hormones in plants.

objectives.text: Match endocrine glands to the hormones they secrete
Compare nervous and hormonal coordination
Explain the effects of hormone deficiency and the role of plant hormones

topics.name: Evolution
topics.summary: The theories that explain how species change over time and the evidence that supports them.

subtopics.name: Theories of Evolution
subtopics.summary: Lamarck, Darwin and the modern account of natural selection.

objectives.text: Outline Lamarck's theory and explain why it was rejected
Explain Darwin's theory of natural selection step by step
Apply natural selection to examples such as antibiotic resistance

subtopics.name: Evidence for Evolution
subtopics.summary: Fossils, homologous structures, embryology and adaptive radiation as lines of evidence.

objectives.text: Describe the fossil record as evidence for evolution
Distinguish homologous, analogous and vestigial structures
Explain adaptive radiation with a named example

provenance.note: Tier A Biology tree covering the WAEC, NECO and JAMB core syllabus.
